## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Fix the duplicate adoption output: any command run that adopts an existing setting now prints each "Adopted" line twice, because the new `adopt` entries reach a CLI loop that only skips `audit` entries.

## Changes
`plan` now returns an `adopt` entry for each setting that already exists, in addition to emitting progress, and adds a final `audit` entry recording how many settings were processed. The PR adds two CLI tests for the audit entry and a new `app/review.txt` file.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/planner.py:9 — correctness — Stop the CLI from re-emitting adopt entries — When `run({"theme": "dark"}, {"theme": "dark"}, emit)` adopts a setting, `emit` receives `["Adopted theme", "Adopted theme"]`. `plan` emits the progress line at `app/planner.py:8`, and the new `adopt` entry reaches `app/cli.py:6-9`, which emits every non-`audit` change. No test calls `run` with an existing setting. — Every adopted setting appears twice in command output, which contradicts the PR body's claim that the command renders only actionable changes. — Fix: Skip `kind == "adopt"` alongside `audit` at `app/cli.py:7`, and add a `run` adoption test next to `test_adoption_progress` that asserts `messages == ["Adopted theme"]`.
